trigger: An operator command fails before the intended runtime gate, including 404 source lookup, malformed PowerShell tokens, missing downloaded files, blocked child executable launch, terminal closure, lost visible diagnostics, or a paste/display anomaly such as unexpected question-mark glyphs.

steps.action: Classify the earliest observed failure boundary: source-resolution, transport-corruption, input-capture, presentation-rendering-unproven, shell-control, child-executable-launch, prerequisite-missing, downstream-runtime, or evidence-resolution.
steps.gate: One boundary is named without promoting downstream proof; Access is denied before the downstream artifact is child-executable-launch, and a visible glyph alone is not transport-corruption.

steps.action: For a paste/display anomaly, run scripts/Inspect-OperatorTerminalPasteBoundary.ps1 before changing terminal settings. Preserve only its local evidence artifact, not raw clipboard text.
steps.gate: The artifact reports literal question-mark/replacement-character counts or captured-input-clean-presentation-unproven; clean captured input leaves font, terminal, PSReadLine, and WezTerm presentation unproven.

steps.action: Preserve the failed command and exact stderr/stdout as local operational evidence; do not commit operator-machine data.
steps.gate: Failure evidence is available for comparison.

steps.action: Re-resolve the requested repository ref and every required file independently of the failed command.
steps.gate: The source exists or the exact missing ref/file is identified.

steps.action: Resolve the exact executable path at the failed child boundary and run the bounded child-executable launch probe before retrying the downstream wrapper.
steps.gate: A child-executable-launch-result artifact identifies passed, blocked, timed-out, or child-nonzero without requiring the downstream runtime.

steps.action: Run the focused command-delivery validator against the repaired command form and regression fixtures.
steps.gate: Transport, input-boundary, shell-control, and blocked-child-launch fixtures behave deterministically.

steps.action: Repair harness maps, workflows, registries, skill, report, hook, or validators when the failure class was not already enforced.
steps.gate: A fresh agent can discover the trap before reproducing it.

steps.action: Commit and push the harness repair on an isolated branch; open or update the owning PR.
Only after harness validation and successful required executable launch proof, provide the smallest executable operator command that advances to the previously unproven runtime gate.
steps.gate: The command preserves the parent terminal and prints both the child-launch artifact and canonical downstream artifact.

stopConditions: Source ref or required file cannot be resolved.
A required external executable is present but cannot be concretely launched; stop at child-executable-launch until that workstation boundary is repaired.
Repair would require product-code mutation outside the declared lane.
The next proof requires credentials, protected runtime access, destructive reset, or another unauthorized capability.
proofCeiling: Failure classification, read-only captured-input evidence, concrete child-executable launch evidence, and harness repair only. Clean captured input does not prove presentation correctness; runtime success must be earned again from the downstream owning artifact.
